CLIMATE CHANGE • ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY

One Change.
Many Systems.

Climate change does not affect only one part of our world. It can influence ecosystems, water, food, cities and human health — all connected.

Explore the science → Open climate map
When the climate changes, nature responds.

Explore the real-world connections below.

01 / WHY IT MATTERS

It is all
connected.

A warmer and changing climate can create pressure that moves through natural and human systems. A change in temperature can influence water availability, habitats, agriculture, infrastructure and health. Understanding these connections helps us make better decisions.

01One climate change signal can affect multiple systems.
05Key systems explored on RE:EARTH.
∞Connections between people and the environment.
02 / SEE THE CONNECTION

Three stories.
One changing climate.

Scroll through real-world examples to see how climate-related pressures can appear in different environments and communities.

01 — HEAT & FIRE

When heat reaches ecosystems.

Heat, dryness and wildfire can place pressure on vegetation and wildlife. The effects can spread through habitats and biodiversity.

ECOSYSTEMS • WILDLIFE
02 — WATER & FOOD

When water becomes harder to depend on.

Changes in rainfall and water availability can affect landscapes, agriculture and the animals that depend on those environments.

WATER • FOOD • LIVELIHOODS
03 — ICE & HABITAT

When a habitat starts to change.

Warming environments can alter the conditions that species depend on. Climate change therefore becomes a biodiversity and habitat issue.

ICE • HABITAT • BIODIVERSITY

Climate impacts
reach people too.

Environmental hazards can disrupt homes, transport, infrastructure and essential services. Climate awareness is also about understanding community resilience.
